test_title: SSC MTS 2023 Official Paper (Held On: 14 Sept 2023 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: A 228 m long train is running at 125 km/h. In what time (in seconds), will it pass a man running at 17 km/h in the same direction in which the train is going?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Relative Speed** in same direction = 125 − 17 = 108 km/h.

Convert to m/s: 108 × (5/18) = 6 × 5 = 30 m/s.

**Time taken** = Train Length ÷ Relative Speed = 228 ÷ 30 = 7.6 sec.

**∴ The correct answer is 7.6 sec.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of **train** = 228 m

Speed of **train** (V₁) = 125 km/h

Speed of **man** (V₂) = 17 km/h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/769ef146bbb605bc205672cc974117dc18750830209f8dabde095afd68d14f57.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

Relative Speed (Same Direction) = Speed of Train − Speed of Man

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative Speed = 125 − 17 = 108 km/h

⇒ To convert km/h to m/s: 108 × (5/18) m/s

⇒ Relative Speed = 6 × 5 = 30 m/s

⇒ Distance to be covered = Length of train = 228 m

⇒ Time = 228 ÷ 30

⇒ Time = 7.6 sec

**∴ The correct answer is 7.6 sec.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two objects move in the same direction, the relative speed is found by **subtracting** the slower speed from the faster speed (S₁ − S₂).

Relative Speed in Opposite Direction

When two objects move toward each other or in opposite directions, the relative speed is the **sum** of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂).

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from **km/h to m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert from **m/s to km/h**, multiply by 18/5.

Distance for Crossing

When a train crosses a **man, pole, or tree**, the distance is the length of the train. If it crosses a **platform or bridge**, distance = Length of train + Length of platform.</p
